title: La dame de France 2  (The France 2 Lady)

segments.t: On the movie set, veteran actor Guy Marchand finishes a take and meets Elisabeth Lecoeur, an executive from France 2 Cinema. When Elisabeth reveals that a committee meets tomorrow to decide on funding Julien Dore's project, Gabriel seizes the opportunity to invite her to lunch. Listen to the scene in French first.
Enchanté! Gabriel Sarda est mon agent.
Et notre réalisateur est très talentueux.
On décide si on finance son film.
Je peux vous inviter à déjeuner?
Let's walk through the conversation step by step.
'Everything is going very well, thanks!' Literally 'all goes very well', this upbeat reply closes on the everyday French word meaning 'thanks' — a cousin of English 'mercy'.
'Bravo Guy, what a wonderful role!' Exclamations opening with 'what' in French never add 'a' — word-for-word, Elisabeth says 'what fine role!'.
'Elisabeth Lecoeur, from France 2 Cinema.' Notice her surname: many French family names fuse 'the' onto an everyday word — hers literally means 'the heart'.
Enchanté! Gabriel Sarda est mon agent.
'Delighted! Gabriel Sarda is my agent.' Literally 'enchanted!', that single-word opener is what you'd say whenever you are introduced to someone new.
'France 2 is financing this fine film.' One pointer word in French covers both 'this' and 'that' ahead of 'fine film', while 'finances' is a direct cognate.
'It is normal, it is your money!' Saying 'it is normal' in French means 'naturally!' or 'that makes total sense', and the word meaning 'money' literally means 'silver'.
'There, you know Guy Marchand!' Built from 'see' plus 'there', that lively opener uses French's dedicated action for knowing people and places rather than facts.
'I really loved the screenplay.' In French film talk, what looks like English 'scenario' means 'screenplay' or 'script'.
Et notre réalisateur est très talentueux.
'And our director is very talented.' Here 'director' ends in '-teur' for a man rather than '-trice', paired with a close cognate of 'talented'.
'And how is Julien Dore doing?' Asking 'how goes' works for any person's name, and the singer-actor's real surname literally means 'golden' in French.
'The committee meets tomorrow.' Literally 'the commission reunites itself tomorrow' — French happily pairs the present with 'tomorrow' for scheduled meetings.
On décide si on finance son film.
'We decide whether we finance his film.' One tiny two-letter word covers both 'if' and 'whether' in French, bridging the two halves cleanly.
'Now, I am stressing a lot!' Placed right at the start of a reaction, the word that usually means 'there' shifts in spoken French to mean 'hearing that, right now!'.
'Are you in a hurry this noon?' French says 'are you pressed?' for being in a rush, and 'this noon' is the everyday expression meaning 'this lunchtime'.
Je peux vous inviter à déjeuner?
'Can I invite you to lunch?' Careful in France: 'inviting' someone to a meal promises you are paying the bill, and 'lunch' comes from 'breaking a fast'! Now let's listen to the whole dialogue again.
Enchanté! Gabriel Sarda est mon agent.
Et notre réalisateur est très talentueux.
On décide si on finance son film.
Je peux vous inviter à déjeuner?
After introducing Guy Marchand to Elisabeth Lecoeur, Gabriel uses the chance encounter to invite the television executive to lunch. See you next time!
